title: Microscopic theory of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in nonmagnetic-metal/ferromagnetic-metal heterostructures
abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) in nonmagnetic-metal/ferromagnetic-metal heterostructures. Tracing out the conduction-electron degrees of freedom in the FM, we derive an effective interfacial exchange coupling between the localized spins and the conduction electron spins in the adjacent electron system. Based on this interaction, we calculate the current-induced driving torque, resonance-frequency shift, damping modulation, and resulting dc voltage. As a concrete example, we apply the formulation to a disordered Rashba two-dimensional electron gas and demonstrate that the ST-FMR spectrum reflects the dynamical spin responses of the adjacent electron system. Our formulation applies to a broad class of heterostructures and establishes a unified microscopic framework connecting ST-FMR spectra directly to the electronic spin responses of adjacent systems.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive microscopic theory for Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance in NM/FM interfaces. It derives the current-induced torque and resulting dc voltage by treating the coupling between localized spins and conduction electrons. The key achievement is establishing a unified framework that links measurable magnetic resonance spectra directly to the electronic spin dynamics of the adjacent nonmagnetic metal.
main_problem: The paper develops a microscopic theory to explain Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) in nonmagnetic-metal/ferromagnetic-metal (NM/FM) heterostructures.
main_result: The theory successfully connects the measured dc voltage in ST-FMR directly to the electronic spin responses (susceptibility and conductivity) of the adjacent nonmagnetic system.
method: The approach uses Green's function techniques, integrating out conduction electron degrees of freedom to derive effective interfacial exchange couplings and calculating observables via linear response theory.
model_or_system: The system is an NM/FM heterostructure. The model incorporates the s-d exchange Hamiltonian, treating the FM spins via spin-wave approximations and the NM response using advanced Green's function formalism, including Rashba SOC effects.
key_observables: dc voltage ($V_{dc}$), resonance-frequency shift ($\delta\omega_0$), damping modulation ($\delta\alpha_G$), and the Rashba–Edelstein conductivity ($\sigma_{REE}$).
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the effective magnetic fields ($\mathbf{h}_Y(\omega), \mathbf{h}_Z(\omega)$) and the frequency ($\omega$) of the applied microwave field.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on linear-response theory, the random averaging of couplings, and the use of the rotating-wave approximation for spin dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ST-FMR setup and $V_{dc}$ spectrum, the role of damping-like and field-like torques, band structures showing spin splitting, and the frequency dependence of the resonance shift and damping modulation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general Hamiltonian, then deriving the effective interfacial coupling by integrating out FM electrons, and finally applying this framework to calculate specific observables like the dc voltage and spin susceptibility using advanced Green's function techniques.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of linear response theory, Green's functions, and the explicit calculation of dynamic susceptibilities ($\chi(\omega)$) mirrors techniques used in open quantum systems and quantum transport theory.
